answer.evidence: Both boulders show a lighter, foreshortened top plane that steps sharply to a dark front face. In the left boulder at x=9, light rows 13-18 (L=141) drop to dark rows 19-26 (L=51 down to 31). In the right boulder at x=23, light rows 19-21 (L=144) drop through rows 22-23 to dark rows 24-27. The silhouette widens from 3px at row 11 to 29px at rows 22-23, which gives a rounded mass. The main body is the left boulder, with a top of about 7 rows and a front of about 8 rows. This matches the green 'top plus front' references, not the flat or rim-only red ones.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is two small grey boulders with about 3 lightness steps each (light top face, mid body, dark underside) plus a dark outline. It has 6 raw colours in total, and the 6 visible tones per tile are close to tree-1a786c's 7. Against tree-d43edd's 29 visible tones, and by eye against both references, it is much simpler. The 0% near-flat figure is misleading, because the faces are small, smooth blobs with no stone grain, no cracks, no per-facet highlights and no moss or grass blending at the base. 40% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is mixed, partly a neutral dark line giving a sticker look, rather than a consistent dark tone of the rock. The pair is also noticeably smaller and thinner than a full 2x2-tile prop. Placed next to the richly clumped, multi-tone references, it looks flatter and more sticker-like.
